text.content:
A ship is any vessel over 50 m long and 100 tonnes; anything smaller is a boat (the small craft are vehicle actors in the Cyberpirates Vehicles compendium). Ships use ship ratings in place of some vehicle attributes (p.162–163):

  • Speed (Cavitation): the number in parentheses is the Cavitation Threshold. Faster than that, the propellers' noise lowers the ship's Sonar Signature (easier to find and hit by sonar and torpedoes; p.169). Speed × 1.54 = knots. Boats have no Cavitation Threshold.
  • Hull replaces Body, on a larger scale: 1 = 100–200 tonnes, 2 = 201–500, 3 = 501–1,000, 4 = 1,001–5,000, 5 = 5,001–10,000, 6 = 10,001–25,000, 7 = 25,000–50,000, 8 = 50,001–100,000, 9 = 100,001–250,000, 10+ = over 250,000.
  • Bulwark replaces Armor in ship combat (to convert Hull and Bulwark to Armor or Barrier Ratings, see Ramming, p.164–165).
  • Signature "N/M": normal Signature (radar, thermographic and other sensors) / Sonar Signature.
  • Sonar: the ship's sonar and contact-analysis capability (Sensors and Sonar, p.168).
  • Depth (submarines and minisubs): the safe maximum depth in meters; deeper, the hull takes crush damage (p.168).
  • Accommodation replaces Seating: the crew and passengers the ship can house.
  • Load works as for vehicles (Rigger 2 p.24). Ship electronics add Hull × 5 to their Flux Rating, but surface-to-surface scanning, jamming and communication stops at the 35 km horizon line.

The ship rules themselves (crews, ship combat, ramming, damage control, sonar, thermoclines) are not automated: run them from the book. Cyberpirates p.162–163.
